correctness.rationale: Campbell’s double sum is partitioned by \(a=0\) and \(a>0\). On \(a=0\), Kummer/Legendre gives the exact summand valuation \(3A-2s_2(n)\), yielding residue \(4\) only at one-bit indices. For \(a>0\), an odd squared middle binomial forces disjoint binary supports; the position \(\nu_2(a)\) then gives at least two carries in one remaining binomial coefficient, so every summand is divisible by \(4\). Pairing under \(b\leftrightarrow n-3a-b\) kills nonfixed terms modulo \(8\), and Lucas’ theorem classifies the only surviving fixed point as \((a,b,n)=(2^k,0,3\cdot2^k)\). Exact replay checks all formulas on large finite ranges without being used as an infinite proof.
